topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the core learning objectives on cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic, Environmental, and Epidemiological Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the interplay between endogenous mutational processes, environmental exposures, and epidemiological patterns in determining cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as an example of pathogen-associated oncogenesis.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA, including direct modification and activation via xenobiotic metabolism.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility Contexts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors, including tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental stages, cooperate with initiators to facilitate cancer progression.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and test their mutagenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by discussing practical risk-benefit balances regarding exposure and summarizing the overarching themes of cancer causation.
